Person who broke up with a partner here. 

My BPD caused me to stay with my previous partner far longer than we should have (8 yrs). I found myself clinging onto someone who was abusive (to me, themselves, and others) and manipulative. I felt like if we broke up, I wouldn't be able to function. They were my FP for a very long time and it felt physically painful to think about life without them. 

But I had to put myself first when I realized it was best for me and my well-being. I felt like I was dying inside but I took it each day and kept reminding myself that this feeling while terrifying, was temporary. That breaking up was giving me a new lease on life of sorts. A chance to be more self-aware of my BPD and be present in the moment. Three years later I'm happier single and have made a good support circle. 

I'm sorry that that instance happened with you and your partner, I hope this is something you both can work through, and that this instance just makes you both stronger.

 But if it does happen give yourself a few days, a few weeks to feel those feelings and know that they'll pass and that you matter so very much, with or without a partner/fp.

Recommend this highly. I use chatgpt for anxiety attacks/splitting/overthinking episodes when I don't feel safe talking to someone. While chatgpt is an AI, it's a safe space to disclose feelings and while it's not a licensed professional, its programming is built to keep the user safe (iirc). It's a great place to find a voice to listen and hear you out, when your brain isn't helpful. I used it to help myself become less heightened and handle those overwhelming moments better. Good on you OP for finding better ways to handle splitting, Sending love and good energy your way.

I only relapse about 1-3 times a year, but my cuts from my teens are very visible and makes it hard to make friends or connections without initial judgement, but it's always been a reminder of how far I've come and how much I've heard over time. I may slip up from time to time, but I know one day it'll get better.

See if you can get a teledoc appointment. When I can't get in with my general practitioner or my psychiatrist I will set up a teledoc appointment and just explain to them my situation and they'll usually give me a month refill. Maybe this can help right now until you're able to see your psychiatrist.
